section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1976
title: The incidence of: suicides for the Union Territories as a whole recorded an increase of 2.3 percent in 1976 over the total number of suicides recorded in the Union Territories during 1975. Arunachal Pradesh did not record any change. Three Union Territories recorded a decline and these were Lakshadweep (66.7 percent), Pondicherry (26.0 percent) and Goa, Daman & Diu (6.2 percent). The Union Territories which recorded an increase were Mizoram (250.0 percent), A & N Islands (208.7 percent), Chandigarh (61.5 percent), D & N Haveli (41.7 percent) and Delhi (17.6 percent). The incidence of suicides for the Metropolitan Cities as a whole recorded a decline of 15.7 percent in 1976 over 1975 figures. Out of 8 Metropolitan Cities, four recorded a decline in 1976 over 1975 and these were Madras (40.5 percent), Hyderabad (36.0 percent), Kanpur (18.7 percent) and Bangalore (13.2 percent). The Metropolitan Cities which recorded an increase were Bombay (27.4 percent), Ahmedabad (26.4 percent), Delhi (13.2 percent) and Calcutta (7.3 percent). The overall decrease recorded for Metropolitan Cities as a whole was much more than the all-India average which was only 3.4 percent. The details are presented in Table 4.
